Clean-room training certifications are offered by organizations such as the National Environmental Balancing Bureau (NEBB) or Controlled Environmental Regulatory Testing Services (CERTS). In relation to building and maintaining the cleanroom environment, the Associated Air Balance Page 19 of 55 “Manufacturing full-scale high gradient copper accelerators: Electron beam welding and allied processes” Prepared for the U.S. Department of Energy ARDAP program Council (AABC) also offers certification for test and balance engineers and technicians who are responsible for building and maintaining high-quality air purification systems for cleanrooms. Cleanroom credentials are commonly required for industries such as mechatronics, semiconductor manufacturing, and surgical/medical equipment manufacturing, bio/pharma, and operating room preparation. Personnel involved in the cleanroom operations at a high-gradient structure fabrication facility can be acquired by performing a hiring search on applicants with cleanroom experience or prior certification as a pre-requisite. However, the bulk of the technical skill and know-how to perform cleaning and surface preparation procedures for high-gradient structure fabrication can be learned through on-the-job training and by establishing robust standard operating procedures (SOPs) for cleanroom personnel.
